弔.meaning: When the old archer dies, her friends lash her <part>bow</part> to a tall <part>pole</part> at the village gate, its string loose and a black ribbon tied round it. All week people stop by, pat the pole and leave a kind note for her grandson. The pole fills up with <kanji>condolences</kanji>.
弔.on: Her grandson wears her old bead <sound>cho</sound>ker under his collar, in her memory.
弔.kun: The village carves her a <sound>to</sound>tem pole, a cow bows with a soft '<sound>Mu</sound>', and the cook serves bowls of <sound>ra</sound>men in her name.

倉.meaning: A hungry building at the docks has an <part>umbrella</part> roof and a wide <part>mouth</part> for a door. Each morning the boss raises a <part>flag</part>, paints <part>one</part> <part>slash</part> on the wall for every ship, and the mouth swallows crates of tea and rope until dark. Sailors call this warehouse a <kanji>godown</kanji>.
倉.on: Its floor is so clean that the night guard polishes it with a bar of <sound>so</sound>ap.
倉.kun: A <sound>coo</sound>k sneaks in after dark to borrow a crate of <sound>ra</sound>men noodles.

荘.meaning: A <part>robust</part> old sailor retires to the hills and builds a cabin with a roof of thick green <part>grass</part>. Goats graze on top while he lies in a hammock below with lemonade. Friends come for long holidays. It's a little cabin, but he calls it his <kanji>villa</kanji>.
荘.on: Guests wash in an outdoor tub with a bar of <sound>so</sound>ap as big as a brick.
荘.kun: He waters the roof with a garden <sound>ho</sound>se, then locks the gate with a big brass <sound>key</sound>.

汁.meaning: A stingy cook drops <part>ten</part> peas into a pot of <part>water drops</part> and stirs. Ten guests arrive with ten spoons. Each one fishes out exactly one pea, sips the hot water and smiles politely. It's mostly water, but he calls it <kanji>soup</kanji>.
汁.on: One guest finds a <sound>jew</sound>el at the bottom of her bowl instead of a pea.
汁.kun: A <sound>shee</sound>p laps up the leftovers, and a <sound>roo</sound>k drinks straight from the ladle.

殴.meaning: A polite <part>maiden</part> in a frilly skirt curtseys to the bully who has been stealing lunches all over the <part>ward</part>, then swings her heavy handbag and knocks his hat into the fountain. Shocked shopkeepers call it <kanji>assault</kanji>; the rest of the block calls her a hero.
殴.on: The bully hides up an <sound>o</sound>ak tree until she has gone home.
殴.kun: Up there he nibbles a <sound>na</sound>an, while a <sound>goo</sound>se honks at him from below.

乞.meaning: A seal sits at the end of the <part>diving board</part> at the public pool, flapping and barking at every swimmer with a sandwich. When nobody shares, it slides down the <part>zigzag</part> water slide and tries again from the top. All afternoon it does nothing but <kanji>beg</kanji>.
乞.on: A <sound>ko</sound>ala lifeguard sneezes, '<sound>Tsu</sound>!', and drops it a crust.
乞.kun: Next it begs a sleepy <sound>ko</sound>ala on a towel for the rest of its lunch.
